verdict: Grainger's sales rose 11% as demand improved across both businesses, and strong operating leverage let it raise its full-year outlook.

segments.name: High-Touch Solutions N.A.
segments.note: Maintenance and repair products sold with dedicated sales teams and on-site services, about $4.1 billion per the earnings call.

segments.name: Endless Assortment
segments.note: Online-only Zoro (U.S.) and MonotaRO (Japan), selling a huge catalog with no sales reps.

opex.name: Sales, general & admin
opex.note: Sales teams, distribution network support, marketing and the back office.

otherDetail: Net interest expense of $21 million, partly offset by $7 million of other income, for a net $14 million cost.
follow100Note: Kept as profit is total net earnings of $616 million; $587 million of it belongs to Grainger shareholders and $29 million to noncontrolling interests (mainly MonotaRO's minority owners).

takeaways.title: Underlying growth is even faster
takeaways.text: On a daily, organic constant-currency basis sales grew 14.9% — the reported 11.3% is held back by the exit from the U.K. market.

takeaways.title: Margins expanded on volume
takeaways.text: Adjusted operating margin rose to 16.1% as double-digit volume growth spread fixed costs, lifting adjusted operating earnings 18% to $836 million.

takeaways.title: Full-year outlook raised
takeaways.text: Grainger now expects 2026 sales of $19.8-20.0 billion and adjusted EPS of $47.00-48.00, up from $45.50-47.25.

oneTimers: Reported operating earnings include $8 million of transaction costs for the Adroit technology acquisition; adjusted operating earnings of $836 million exclude them.
Year-ago results included a large loss on the exit of the U.K. market, which is why reported operating earnings appear to jump 62% — the adjusted increase is 18%.
